1#_: Or of glass. Be'er Heitev and Beit Yosef; Ya'avetz siman 60 — all glass vessels of princelings require immersion and a blessing, for they are separated and have a repair through melting; nevertheless, since they are joined, they have a repair to be fit for use, and nevertheless one may rely without immersion because of the loss of the prohibition, as with a father's gift to his son that he may not use on Shabbat — nevertheless the custom is to immerse them without a blessing on weekdays (Erev Pesach and the rest, and in Beit Avraham in Kuntres Aharonim, and they are accustomed to permit without immersion). R' Chaim ruled that vessels that are affixed in a wall for permanence, such as glass vessels affixed in a wall with cement in the wall of a mikveh room, do not require immersion, for they are not vessels at all; and if they are affixed only for permanence of place, such as large glass vessels affixed in a wall with cement in the wall of a mikveh room — requires study. And they are accustomed in our countries to affix glass vessels in a mikveh with cement in the wall of the mikveh room, and they do not immerse them, for they are not vessels; and the custom is to affix them in the wall of the mikveh room with cement, and they are not immersed because they are not vessels — and see Beit Yosef who wrote in the name of Orach Chaim that they require immersion, and nevertheless the custom is to affix the large glass vessels in the mikveh wall with cement and not immerse, as they are not vessels — and see Taz.
2#_: That are coated with lead. Be'er Heitev and Beit Yosef siman 161 — the coating of the inside of a vessel of a non-Jew requires immersion, for the main use is on the inside; and the custom is to immerse without a blessing. And see Taz who wrote like Tur that coating on the inside is only for ornament, and one immerses without a blessing; and the custom is as he wrote there. And see Shach who disagrees and requires immersion with a blessing if coated inside and outside, as it is like metal vessels.
3#_: Requires immersion. Be'er Heitev and Beit Yosef chapter 3 daf 75b — that a non-Jew bought vessels from a Jew and returned them, if the Jew had not used them for a meal but for cards, he need not immerse; but if he used them for a meal, he requires immersion. And see Taz and Shach who disagree on this. And see Maharsha who explains that the reason of Tosafot at the end — "but one who pledges a vessel to a non-Jew and returned and redeemed it does not require immersion" — is because now that he redeemed it we see that initially he did not truly intend to sink it; but beforehand it is fine to be uncertain lest he intended to sink it, and if so he requires immersion in any case without a blessing; unlike if the reason is because we establish that a non-Jew does not acquire a pledge from a Jew — if so, it is the Jew's from beginning to end; requires study.
